title: ておく vs てしまう: helper verb secrets
summary: Japanese uses many specific helper verbs where English uses up and out. ておく puts an action in place for a purpose; てしまう says it just happened.

blocks.text: English leans on little words like **up** and **out**: eat up, think up, cry out, lose out. Japanese has no prepositions at all. It uses **helper verbs** instead, and since there are many more of them, each one is more precise. So when you meet a helper verb you do not recognize, ask what picture its own verb carries.
Here is a puzzle sentence. Nothing is being put down anywhere, so why does it have おく?

blocks.jp: 先生には、私から話しておきます。
blocks.en: I will tell the teacher myself (so it is taken care of).

blocks.text: The answer is the picture of おく: you do something now and **leave it in place** for later. Keep that picture in mind through the lesson.
ておく: put the action in place

**おく** means to put or set something down. A **て-form + おく** puts an action in place, usually **for a purpose**, so that the situation will then be the way you want. (As lesson 21 showed, it can also just leave the result in place.) It feels like the work of a careful workman, with no exclamation mark.

blocks.en: (I) open the window (and leave it so the room gets air).

blocks.jp: 先に皆に説明しておきます。
blocks.en: I will explain to everyone beforehand (so nobody is in the dark).

blocks.jp: 旅行の前に切符を買っておいた。
blocks.en: I bought the ticket before the trip (to be ready).

blocks.text: てしまう: it ended up done
**しまう** means to finish or put away, and the helper adds an **exclamation mark**: it happened, whether or not you expected or wanted it ("I done fell over"). It is often unwelcome, but not always.

blocks.jp: 財布を忘れてしまった。
ケーキを全部食べてしまった。

blocks.text: The same verb with each helper tells a different story. 説明しておく is careful preparation. 説明してしまう is going ahead and explaining regardless, perhaps at length and unasked.

blocks.jp: さくらには、私が説明しておく。
blocks.en: I will explain it to Sakura (so she is prepared).

blocks.jp: 質問しないで。さくらが長く説明してしまうから。
blocks.en: Don't ask her. Sakura will go on and explain at length.

rows: Finish it, with an exclamation mark
切符をなくしてしまった。

blocks.text: In casual speech both helpers shrink: **〜とく** for ておく, **〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう** for てしまう.

blocks.jp: 明日までに、この本を読んどく。
blocks.en: I will read this book by tomorrow (to be ready).

items: **ておく**: do it ahead, for a purpose, to set things up.
**てしまう**: it got done or happened, with a feeling of "there, it happened".
Casual: 見ておく → 見とく; 食べてしまった → 食べちゃった.
Learn helper verbs as pictures, not as English words.

questions.instruction: What does おく add?
questions.prompt: 試験の前に、ノートを読んでおく。
options: Doing it ahead, for a purpose
questions.en: (I) read my notes before the exam (to be prepared).
questions.note: ておく puts the action in place so things are ready.

questions.instruction: What does しまう add?
questions.prompt: 電車の中で、かさを忘れてしまった。
questions.en: Oops, I left my umbrella on the train.
questions.note: てしまう adds an exclamation mark: it got done, whether wanted or not.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 忘れないように、メモを書いて＿＿＿。
questions.en: So I won't forget, I wrote a note (beforehand).
questions.note: A purpose (so as not to forget) calls for ておく.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: あ、大事な写真を消して＿＿＿！
questions.en: Oh no, I deleted the important photo!
questions.note: An unwelcome accident calls for てしまう.

questions.instruction: Which is the casual form of 見ておく?
questions.note: ておく shrinks to とく.

questions.instruction: Which is the casual form of 食べてしまった?
questions.note: てしまう shrinks to ちゃう.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I'll leave the heater on (so the room stays warm)"?
options: ヒーターをつけてしまう。
ヒーターをつけておく。
ヒーターをつけてくる。
ヒーターをつけている。
questions.note: Setting things up for a purpose is ておく.

questions.instruction: Which sentence feels like an unwelcome accident?
options: お茶をこぼしてしまった。
questions.note: こぼしてしまった: it spilled, oops.

questions.instruction: Tap the helper verb that sets things up ahead
questions.en: (I) will make tomorrow's breakfast ahead of time.
questions.note: おく is the helper verb that puts the action in place.

questions.instruction: Tap the helper verb that carries the "oops" feeling
questions.note: しまった adds the exclamation mark.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.note: て-form + おく: done ahead for a purpose.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: Oh no, I lost my phone.
questions.en: Oh no, I lost my phone.
questions.note: て-form + しまった: it happened, oops.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: (I) will clean the room before the guests arrive.
questions.en: (I) will clean the room before the guests arrive.
questions.note: Preparing in advance is ておく.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I'll tell him in advance (so he is prepared)"?
questions.note: The careful workman's helper is おく.

questions.instruction: Which picture does おく carry?
options: Putting something in place for a purpose
questions.note: おく means to put or set something down.

questions.instruction: Which picture does しまう carry?
options: Finishing or putting away, with an exclamation mark
questions.note: しまう means to finish or put away.

questions.instruction: True or false? てしまう is always about something unwelcome.
questions.note: It is often unwelcome, but not always: ケーキを全部食べてしまった-type sentences can be happy.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: ピザを一人で全部食べて＿＿＿。
questions.en: I ate the whole pizza all by myself.
questions.note: Finishing it all, with a "there, it happened" feeling.

questions.instruction: Which is the casual form of 飲んでしまった?
questions.note: After ん the casual form is じゃう.

questions.instruction: Which helper verb sounds like a careful workman, with no exclamation mark?
questions.note: おく prepares quietly.

questions.instruction: Which is the full form of 忘れちゃった?
questions.note: ちゃった is the casual てしまった.

questions.instruction: Which means ドアを開けとく?
questions.note: とく is the casual ておく.
